classification.difficultyReason: Interpret heights relative to eye level and apply tangent or inverse tangent.

content.prompt: Carlos is standing $16\text{ m}$ from the base of a tree that is $14\text{ m}$ high. Carlos’s eye is $1.6\text{ m}$ from the ground.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the angle of elevation from Carlos’s eye to the top of the tree, correct to the nearest degree?

answer.worked:
The vertical distance above Carlos’s eye is $14-1.6=12.4\text{ m}$. Let the angle of elevation be $\theta$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{12.4}{16}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{12.4}{16}\right)\\\theta&\approx38^\circ\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: If Carlos looks up at an angle of $26^\circ$, how far up the tree will he see? Give your answer correct to the nearest centimetre.

answer.worked:
Let $y\text{ m}$ be the vertical distance above Carlos’s eye and $h\text{ m}$ the height above the ground.
$$\begin{align*}\tan26^\circ&=\frac{y}{16}\\y&=16\tan26^\circ\\h&=1.6+16\tan26^\circ\\h&\approx9.40\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: What is the angle of elevation from Carlos’s eye to a point halfway up the tree, correct to the nearest degree?

answer.worked:
Halfway up the tree is $14\div2=7\text{ m}$ above the ground, so the vertical distance above Carlos’s eye is $7-1.6=5.4\text{ m}$. Let the angle of elevation be $\theta$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{5.4}{16}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{5.4}{16}\right)\\\theta&\approx19^\circ\end{align*}$$
